findings.Quote: She had built the audit site before she died and laid it out for whoever the trigger brought.
findings.Note: This states the deduction outright as narrative fact rather than the character's inference, undercutting the 'read the room' detective beat that precedes it — the prior lines show him reasoning, then this line just tells the conclusion flatly.
findings.Fix: Frame it as his inference: 'She'd built this for whoever the trigger brought — he was sure of it now.'

findings.Quote: written in no incentive to make him behave correctly, because she had already decided he would
findings.Note: tells us her certainty and his character rather than showing evidence for it; reads as an assertion the story hasn't earned yet
findings.Fix: cut the explanation or replace with a concrete detail proving her certainty (a specific clause she omitted, a specific trust she extended)

findings.Quote: a gesture worn so smooth the hand made it without the man
findings.Note: purple abstraction that doesn't survive literal scrutiny — a hand cannot act 'without the man'; it tells us the signature is habitual rather than showing it
findings.Fix: the same tilt and pressure each time, a signature made without thinking

findings.Quote: she tracked the receipts the way you track a thing you always knew was real and never expected to watch cross a table in daylight
findings.Note: Overwrought abstraction that tells the emotion rather than showing it; the simile is vague and doesn't clarify what 'in daylight' physically means here.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; show a concrete physical detail — e.g., 'her eyes moved over each line twice before she let herself blink.'

findings.Quote: "I am the principal for these purposes."
findings.Note: Quire earlier speaks strictly as the broker's representative relaying the broker's preferences (ref 1: "The broker prefers," "the broker would rather know"), consistently distinguishing himself from the broker. Here he abruptly claims to be the principal himself, which contradicts the established relayed-agent framing without any acknowledgment of the shift.
findings.Fix: Have Quire clarify the shift explicitly, e.g. "For logging purposes, treat me as the principal," so it reads as a deliberate legal fiction rather than an unflagged reversal.

findings.Quote: the kind of hiding that ends with priced paper in a private vault
findings.Note: vague noir-flavored phrase that sounds portentous but doesn't literally clarify what 'priced paper in a private vault' means in context; reads as filler mystique rather than concrete stakes
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete specific, e.g. 'hiding that ends with forged instruments locked away where no auditor will ever see them'

findings.Quote: The Compact had no category for a person who wrote the truth in the private language of her own book and then filed none of it.
findings.Note: beat's apparent purpose is a legal-logic reveal, but the claim that omission is categorically outside Compact authority is asserted rather than demonstrated, leaving the deduction feeling stated rather than earned
findings.Fix: add one concrete clause or precedent showing why filing status is the operative boundary, not just declare it

findings.Quote: his face built over forty years of careful habits around the knowledge that he was not big enough to win an argument with his own body
findings.Note: convoluted abstraction that tells rather than shows character/physicality, and strains under literal parsing (a face 'built' around 'knowledge')
findings.Fix: His face carried forty years of a small man's caution — the habits of someone who'd learned early he couldn't win a fight with his own body.

findings.Quote: Forty years of carrying a figure he could never say out loud, and then, at last, someone else saying it for him.
findings.Note: Reads as a summarizing, pseudo-profound statement of emotional significance rather than a dramatized moment; tells the reader how to feel about backstory not yet earned on the page.
findings.Fix: Trim to a more concrete beat, e.g. 'Forty years he'd never said the number aloud. Vig just had.'

findings.Quote: a non-evidentiary finding needed no entry, and he made one anyway
findings.Note: stated rule and action directly conflict without explanation, and no reason is given for the deviation, making it read as a contradiction rather than characterization
findings.Fix: add a clause grounding why he logs it anyway, e.g. 'anyway, because habit outranked rule'

findings.Quote: They are materially accurate records of what occurred. The absence is the document: the choice not to file these entries was not error or omission. It was the record itself.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphorism stacking; the last three sentences restate the same idea with increasing abstraction rather than adding information, reading as authorial flourish rather than in-world document voice.
findings.Fix: Cut to one assertion: 'The absence from every registry is not an omission. It is the record.'

findings.Quote: eleven pages, Φ14,200 net, settlement marks verified, Section 14 satisfied. The carrier counted the sheets, three plus the attached key
findings.Note: The summary is described as eleven pages, but the carrier counts only three sheets plus a key — these figures don't reconcile without explanation.
findings.Fix: Either change the summary length to match (e.g., 'three pages') or clarify that the eleven-page document was condensed into a three-sheet certified extract.

findings.Quote: On the receipt the letters started child-large and finished small and adult — the same shift in the hand he would later find inside the book.
findings.Note: Forward-referencing detail ('he would later find') breaks the present-tense discovery mode and tips foreshadowing rather than letting it land later.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause after the dash; let the echo register naturally when he opens the book.

findings.Quote: He had been code before he was a body
findings.Note: Slightly precious phrasing that leans toward aphorism-for-effect rather than concrete world detail, though it does carry information.
findings.Fix: Consider grounding it more concretely, e.g. 'He had existed as code for years before the body was grown for him.'

findings.Quote: Room arranged, disposal clause placed, trigger armed — and then she had died and let it fire without her.
findings.Note: the list-then-pivot construction is a common rhythmic crutch; 'let it fire without her' slightly personifies the trigger in a way that verges on stock noir phrasing
findings.Fix: tighten to something more literal: 'Then she had died, and the trigger fired without her.'

findings.Quote: the settled weight of a thing that had been sitting here waiting
findings.Note: 'waiting' objects and 'settled weight' are worn atmospheric filler common to this genre
findings.Fix: cut to concrete sensory detail: dust pattern, scuff marks, temperature difference

findings.Quote: He held there a moment he could not have justified on any bill.
findings.Note: cute aphoristic aside that tells us his professionalism/emotion rather than showing it; slightly undercuts the tension with wit
findings.Fix: cut the line or replace with a physical beat (breath held, latch cold under thumb)

findings.Quote: Not faded, not dirty. Settled into itself.
findings.Note: Vague abstraction stands in for a concrete visual; tells rather than shows the color/texture.
findings.Fix: Name the actual hue it settled into — e.g. 'a flat brown-grey, like tea gone cold.'

findings.Quote: A working object, then — carried, not shelved.
findings.Note: Overt statement of the deduction the preceding sensory details already convey; redundant explanatory tag.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence and let the corner/grease details stand alone.

findings.Quote: the spacing of someone still learning what letters were for
findings.Note: Slightly overwritten explanatory clause telling us what the handwriting means rather than trusting the concrete detail already given.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause and let 'large and a little uneven' stand alone.

findings.Quote: He ran the first ten against the fringe registry. Seven came back as hits, amount and settlement date and witness, all accurate. He ran the next twenty. Eleven verified outright; nine more confirmed through Compact secondary records.
findings.Note: Numbers stack up cleanly (7/10, then 11+9=20/20) reading as tidy exposition rather than investigative texture; the perfect confirmation rate undercuts tension.
findings.Fix: Introduce at least one discrepancy or unresolved entry to break the mechanical accounting.

findings.Quote: The amounts were not small.
findings.Note: Isolated one-line beat is vague filler — tells us scale without any concrete figure or image, functioning as a placeholder rather than a beat.
findings.Fix: Give a concrete number or comparison, or cut and fold the info into the surrounding beat.

findings.Quote: He laid the pen across the page and sat with it.
findings.Note: Generic contemplative gesture that reads as stock 'thinking pose' business rather than a specific, telling action.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more particular physical detail tied to his character or the document.

findings.Quote: Fourteen years of this work had taught him to know a family by its skull.
findings.Note: Tells the reader his expertise rather than showing it through specific observation; reads as an inserted credential rather than perception.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into the jaw-recognition beat: 'He'd learned to read a family in its bones — the Voigt jaw hadn't changed in three generations.'

findings.Quote: She read the book on the table before she read him, and the order of that told him something.
findings.Note: Withholds the actual inference ('told him something') as a vague tease rather than delivering the observation, which reads as coy filler.
findings.Fix: State what it told him: 'She read the book on the table before she read him — she'd come for the ledger, not the man.'

findings.Quote: rehearsed past the point where she still believed they'd work
findings.Note: Tells the reader her emotional state (loss of belief) rather than showing it through action or subtext; slightly abstract phrasing for a line otherwise grounded in concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a physical tell, e.g. "Her words came out level, the kind of level that takes rehearsal."

findings.Quote: The first silence she had filled because she thought she was supposed to. This one she left alone.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the meaning/motive of both silences rather than letting the contrast register through action; slightly over-explains an already-clear beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause: "The first silence she had filled. This one she left alone."

findings.Quote: let the room hold the rest
findings.Fix: consider a more concrete, less abstract close, e.g. 'and said nothing more.'

findings.Quote: the settled stance of a man who had spent a career letting his body do the negotiating
findings.Note: Vague tough-guy characterization by abstraction rather than concrete detail; tells us he's intimidating without showing anything specific.
findings.Fix: Cut to a concrete physical tell instead of the generalized claim.

findings.Quote: the glance experienced men trade: once, brief, enough
findings.Note: Stock 'knowing look between professionals' beat, vague enough to be filler.
findings.Fix: Specify what the glance actually communicated or cut the aphoristic framing.

findings.Quote: Someone had kept these against a day they knew would come.
findings.Note: Ominous-portent aphorism that tells us meaning/foreboding rather than letting the physical evidence (aging, storage) speak for itself.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with another concrete physical detail about the papers.

findings.Quote: Eleven pages, eleven settled entries in the first forty
findings.Note: the parallel numbers read as a rhetorical flourish rather than a natural audit observation, slightly overpolished for a log-style beat
findings.Fix: Eleven entries settled out of the first forty pages,

findings.Quote: Not a quanta over it, not a quanta under.
findings.Note: the repetition is a stock intensifier construction that reads as filler emphasis rather than earned precision
findings.Fix: Exact, to the quanta.

findings.Quote: Knowing was one register; this was another.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler that states the theme rather than dramatizing it.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete sensory beat showing the gap between knowledge and confrontation.

findings.Quote: He marked it and gave it no weight.
findings.Note: With no stated purpose, this reads as a Chekhov's-gun setup, but the flat delivery ('marked it and gave it no weight') undercuts any tension the detail seems designed to plant.
findings.Fix: Either cut the vehicle detail or let his dismissal carry a beat of doubt to justify its inclusion.

findings.Quote: The knock of someone who had decided before they got there that they would be let in.
findings.Note: Tells the reader how to interpret the knock rather than letting the detail carry it; slightly over-explains an already-clear image.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence and let the single knock stand alone.

findings.Quote: features assembled from half a dozen coastlines and filed under none of them
findings.Note: Purple phrasing that gestures at ambiguity without giving a concrete visual; reads as a stock 'mysterious face' description.
findings.Fix: Replace with one or two specific, contradictory details (e.g., an accent mismatched to a jawline).

findings.Quote: The hands folded on the table, unhurried.
findings.Note: Synecdoche used to avoid naming the speaker reads as affectation rather than clarity; 'unhurried' tells the manner instead of showing it.
findings.Fix: Name the subject or cut the adverb: "He folded his hands on the table."

findings.Quote: he turned the shape of that over once and set it aside
findings.Note: Vague gesture-of-thought filler that tells us he's processing without showing any actual reasoning or conclusion.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete inference or cut.

findings.Quote: "The broker is not a corponation," Quire said.
findings.Note: Stated as a flat assertion with no apparent question or context prompting it, so the exchange reads as disconnected fragments rather than a coherent beat.
findings.Fix: Add a connecting line or attribute the preceding question so the logic chain is visible.

findings.Quote: The question came out already flattened into paperwork.
findings.Note: Vague metaphor — a question can't be physically flattened into a category of document; reads as reaching for texture rather than depicting anything precise.
findings.Fix: The question came out clipped, procedural, as if he were reading it off a form.

findings.Quote: The last line arrived carrying more than it said.
findings.Note: Tells the reader there's subtext rather than trusting the implication already present in dialogue; slightly redundant scaffolding.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence and let the fragments ("Other jobs. Other books.") carry the beat alone.

findings.Quote: He worked through the night.
findings.Note: flat, generic time-passage line that tells rather than shows and adds little given the detailed catalog work that follows
findings.Fix: cut, or fold the time marker into the next beat's opening line

findings.Quote: He set the results down and sat with them.
findings.Note: Vague, low-information gesture standing in for interiority; 'sat with them' is a soft abstraction that tells rather than shows a reaction.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete action that shows his response, e.g. 'He read the list a second time, slower.'

findings.Quote: The shape of the absence was the finding.
findings.Note: Slightly aphoristic phrasing that leans toward pseudo-profound summary rather than concrete detail, though it's grounded by what follows.
findings.Fix: Could be tightened to state the deduction plainly, e.g. 'Nothing existed anywhere. That was the finding.'

findings.Quote: Unless she had never meant them to be instruments.
findings.Note: Fragment functions as vague portentous hook without concrete content; reads as filler suspense rather than earned insight.
findings.Fix: Anchor it to a specific referent so the negation lands: 'Unless she had never meant the ledgers to be instruments at all.'

findings.Quote: a number curdling into a threat
findings.Note: Metaphor strains under literal scrutiny—numbers don't curdle—and edges toward purple phrasing for what is otherwise a precise, restrained passage.
findings.Fix: Consider a plainer verb: 'before the number read as a threat.'

findings.Quote: by morning it had set itself in him without effort
findings.Fix: cut or make concrete: 'by morning he could recite it without looking'

findings.Quote: Three days of one held temperature had made the air feel like a surface.
findings.Note: purple metaphor that doesn't quite parse literally — air 'feeling like a surface' is unclear sensory logic
findings.Fix: clarify what the sensation actually is, e.g. 'The stale, unmoving air pressed at him like a wall.'

findings.Quote: The gap between the structure and the extension is not falsification.
findings.Note: Reads as a slightly too-neat aphoristic legal hairsplit, verging on pseudo-profound phrasing for a private internal justification.
findings.Fix: Ground it more concretely, e.g. specify what document or clause he's measuring against, rather than a clean maxim-like sentence.

findings.Quote: and he did not come alone
findings.Note: Stock ominous-arrival phrasing used often to signal menace.
findings.Fix: Specify who/what accompanied him instead of the stock formulation.

findings.Quote: He regarded the book the way a man regards a dispute he has been patient about for a very long time.
findings.Note: vague comparison that gestures at meaning without specifying what the patience or dispute looks like — tells the emotional stance rather than showing it
findings.Fix: He regarded the book the way a man regards a debt he's decided not to mention again — until he does.

findings.Quote: The breath went out of Vig through his nose — barely there, involuntary, finished before it began.
findings.Note: Over-engineered micro-gesture; the three-part qualifier chain undercuts itself and reads as straining to prove restraint rather than showing it.
findings.Fix: Trim to one or two beats: 'The breath went out of Vig through his nose, involuntary.'

findings.Quote: The pattern of something making sure of a place.
findings.Note: Vague abstraction stands in for the observation itself; tells us it's a pattern of surveillance without grounding the inference in a concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a specific tell, e.g. 'Checking, not passing.'

findings.Quote: A man hearing a number for the first time does not breathe out like that.
findings.Note: Reads as an aphoristic generalization rather than grounded observation, slightly telling rather than showing the deduction.
findings.Fix: Tie it more directly to the specific man/moment: 'Not the breath of a man hearing the number cold.'

findings.Quote: He had never been running from the body.
findings.Note: Abstract aphoristic phrasing that tells rather than shows the character's nature; slightly detached from the immediate action.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a concrete detail, e.g. 'The body was armor, not him.'

findings.Quote: his thumb found the hole before he'd decided to touch anything
findings.Note: telling-not-showing gesture toward involuntary reaction reads as a stock 'body acts before mind' beat without adding specific information
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete observation about the hole's diameter or depth

findings.Quote: But the scope had never been the number.
findings.Note: aphoristic contrast that trades on abstraction ('scope' vs 'the number') without grounding either term concretely in this beat, leaning on portentous vagueness
findings.Fix: specify what 'the scope' and 'the number' refer to so the line lands as insight rather than gnomic filler

findings.Quote: Quire spent two seconds on Renn
findings.Note: Attributing a precise duration to a glance is a slightly clunky mechanic — reads as authorial stage direction rather than observed action.
findings.Fix: Quire glanced at Renn — three days in the same corner...

findings.Quote: Not a challenge. Just certain.
findings.Note: Terse fragment pair tips into telling-not-showing the emotional register of the gesture rather than letting the action carry it.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into the preceding action: his palm settling over Quire's fingers, unhurried, certain.

findings.Quote: not a question, a woman confirming a shape she'd already half traced
findings.Note: abstract, slightly overwrought clarification of tone that tells rather than shows; 'shape half traced' is vague filler imagery
findings.Fix: cut to just the line of dialogue, or replace with something concrete she's confirming

findings.Quote: like someone getting the exact measurements of a room she had already paced out in the dark
findings.Note: purple simile that strains under literal scrutiny — measuring a room 'paced out in the dark' is an odd, overworked image for absorbing information calmly
findings.Fix: simplify to something plainer, e.g. 'like someone confirming what she already knew'

findings.Quote: she said it the way you say a thing you've known was the answer for years and only been waiting to say out loud
findings.Note: pseudo-profound explanatory aside that tells the reader how to feel about the line instead of letting the dialogue carry it
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause and let 'Burn them.' stand alone

findings.Quote: He decoded it the way he'd decoded all the others: amount on the right, source in the center column.
findings.Note: Mechanical restatement of process without new information; reads as filler exposition rather than advancing tension.
findings.Fix: Cut or compress to a single clause focused on what's different this time, not the repeated method.

findings.Quote: a sound that had been in the room four days and that he was only now hearing
findings.Note: The specificity of 'four days' is asserted without grounding; reads as a precise-sounding but unearned detail rather than observed fact.
findings.Fix: Cut to 'a sound that had been there all along' or establish the four-day timeframe earlier.

findings.Quote: she had earned whatever she'd come to see
findings.Note: Vague abstraction stating emotional/narrative weight rather than showing it; reads as a hedge rather than concrete justification.
findings.Fix: Specify what she'd earned or witnessed, e.g., 'she had sat through the worst of it, and she'd stay for the rest.'

findings.Quote: Her jaw was set exactly as it had been on the first day.
findings.Note: Tells the reader continuity of resolve without showing what that expression looked like or means here; relies on the reader recalling an unspecified 'first day' image.
findings.Fix: Specify the concrete detail: 'Her jaw was set, the same tight line it had been the first day she signed.'

findings.Quote: She had known these pages might one day leave the book. She had stitched them to go.
findings.Note: Restates the preceding sentence's information (thread meant to release) as portentous doubled aphorism, telling the reader what to feel rather than adding new information.
findings.Fix: Cut one of the two sentences, or replace the second with a concrete detail (e.g., what she does now that they're gone) rather than restating intent.

findings.Quote: and the page caught and went
findings.Note: vague, slightly euphemistic mechanics for an act the beat wants to land with weight
findings.Fix: and the page caught, curled, and blackened

findings.Quote: Her jaw held.
findings.Note: telling-not-showing shorthand for composure; too compressed to register as characterization
findings.Fix: specify the physical detail that signals restraint, e.g. the muscle at her jaw standing out

findings.Quote: It weighed the sealed notice, then Ledger.
findings.Note: Ambiguous mechanics — 'weighed' applied to a person reads as unintentional double meaning (physical weighing vs. consideration), momentarily confusing subject-object relations.
findings.Fix: It weighed the sealed notice, then considered Ledger.

findings.Quote: the one mark on the page that existed nowhere else in the world
findings.Note: Overreaching abstraction — a signature is not literally unique 'in the world' in a way that supports the quiet, concrete moment; tips toward telling-not-showing significance rather than letting the gesture (thumb along the edge) carry it.
findings.Fix: the one mark on the page that was only his

findings.Quote: when he could no longer hear them he went on listening a while anyway
findings.Note: Borders on a sentimental beat (listening to silence for emotional effect) common enough to edge toward cliché territory, though restrained enough to mostly earn it.
findings.Fix: when he could no longer hear them he stayed still another moment before moving

findings.Quote: It was the most accurate record he could still make of them.
findings.Note: Editorializing summary line that tells the reader how to assess the act rather than letting the detail (the notation itself) carry the weight; slightly softens the documentary precision of the surrounding prose.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence, or replace with a concrete detail (e.g., the exact wording he checked twice).

findings.Quote: The book weighed 380 grams; it had weighed that on the first day, and it weighed that now.
findings.Note: The stated-fact-as-profundity move (weight unchanged despite implied significance) reads as a pseudo-meaningful flourish rather than an earned observation, especially stacked after the corridor silence beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or ground it in a concrete sensory detail tied to the scene rather than stated as a standalone truth.
